method.selection: Within each library sort ascending by SHA256('audit1729:'+item.id), select first 6.
method.presentationOrder: Within selected six sort ascending by SHA256('audit-order1729:'+item.id). Library order l01 to l12.
method.context: Consulted all raw source items to check continuing-context identity. Did not read author labels, other reviews, application code, predictions, or results.
method.scope: Source-supported grouping and dataset adversarial quality only; not an evaluation of app behavior or factual correctness of specialist advice.

summary.assessment: Sampled contexts are supported by specific source evidence. This does not establish correctness of unseen candidate labels. Coverage and repeated phrasing substantially limit claims of generalization.

statistics.quantileConvention: Sorted index floor(p*N), N=360; median reported as sorted index 180.

findings.finding: All 360 inputs fall within 27–37 whitespace words and 160–254 characters. There are no empty or telegraphic captures, long documents, multiple paragraphs, or truncation stress cases.
findings.implication: Results cannot establish sparse-note recovery, long-document identity extraction, mixed-context paragraph handling, or robustness to missing context.

findings.finding: All 360 inputs have kind=text and a single paragraph. Mentions of screenshots, video, photographs and audio are prose rather than supplied media.
findings.implication: This source set cannot establish image/OCR, PDF, audio transcription, video captions, or extraction-path grouping quality.

findings.finding: Many hard-negative and overlapping sources state the intended distinction directly: different projects, separate records, not the other named task. That is legitimate source evidence but an easy linguistic cue.
findings.implication: Success on these explicit examples may overestimate robustness when users omit separation language or merely mention a neighboring project.

findings.finding: Every library includes a source that announces itself as a copied/duplicate reminder and supplies a reason for a second copy.
findings.implication: Repeated duplicate framing is a reusable shortcut; genuine unmarked paraphrases and noisy duplicates need separate coverage.

findings.finding: Corrections frequently tell the reader to retain the earlier note, preserve the old date, or keep contradictory evidence. These are unusually instructional personal notes.
findings.implication: Shared synthetic writing style across development and heldout can correlate reviewer and system decisions without demonstrating real-world temporal identity resolution.

findings.finding: No gold IDs or label-only titles were observed in input fields. Natural source openings repeatedly identify named projects; important omitted-name follow-ups are usually resolvable through unique equipment, places or deliverables.
findings.implication: Natural names are allowed by the contract. They should not be described as label leakage, but uniform title-plus-instruction introductions reduce identity uncertainty.

findings.finding: The sample contains no item for which full-library evidence compels an unresolved choice. Some isolated follow-ups are underspecified, but the supplied library usually contains only one compatible continuing task.
findings.implication: Zero sampled ambiguity is a property of this authored source set, not proof that a reviewer reliably detects ambiguity. Unresolvable pronouns, competing same-task anchors and insufficient evidence remain untested.

findings.finding: Different domains and names reduce direct source overlap, but duplicate-copy, separate-resource coordination, budget tradeoff, correction, and personal-metaphor templates recur across splits.
findings.implication: This raw-source audit cannot certify independence of authoring/paraphrase families. Domain separation alone does not establish stylistic independence.

findings.finding: Multilingual libraries contain English/Spanish and English/French sources with repeated named projects and clear shared nouns. Sampled cross-language identity is supported.
findings.implication: Does not cover transliteration, mixed-language fragments, unrelated scripts, noisy translation, dialects, or source language detection failures.

limitations: Agent-reviewed, not human-validated. This auditor is a separate context, but shared model-family priors and the common contract can create correlated bias.
This was a 20% item audit with full-library context, not an independent review of all candidate labels and not a probability estimate of gold-label error.
No author labels or independent reviewer artifacts were opened during this phase; no claim about their agreement or accuracy is made.
No production code, tuning thresholds, predictions, or results were consulted.
No temporal checkpoint judgments were made; full-library references may use later sources and must not be reused as prefix-time certainty.
Specialist source statements were treated as fictional grouping evidence, without validating operational, scientific, safety, or legal advice.
No missing real-world evidence, new labels, or stricter grouping rules were invented to match any unknown implementation.
